extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO discipline, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and the public interested in USPTO disciplinary actions
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order implementing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on a State disbarment; sets out grounds for exclusion, procedural requirements for notice/response, limited wind-up practice, publication/notice obligations, and compliance requirements for exclusion and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5) (state license revoked on ethical grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) based upon the judgment of a State court disbarring the practitioner for ethical violations (i.e., license to practice law revoked on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice explains the request for exclusion was based on the March 7, 2008 judgment of the Supreme Court of Nebraska disbarring Respondent. The Official Gazette notice repeats that the exclusion is for "violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by having his license to practice law in Nebraska revoked on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State."

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court factual findings supporting discipline (specific misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of Nebraska disbarred Mr. Smith for failure to deposit client's funds in a trust account, failure to account for disbursements from the trust account, and failure to respond to bar counsel's requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites the Nebraska court's conclusions that Mr. Smith violated Code of Professional Responsibility Rule DR 1-102(A)(1) (by violating a Disciplinary Rule); DR 9-102(A)(1) and (2) (failing to preserve the identity of funds and property of the client); Nebraska Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 8.4 (engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice); and violated his oath of office as an attorney. These state-law findings form the factual predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline procedural framework under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order informed Respondent that the OED Director had filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and directed that Respondent could contest imposition of identical discipline by filing a response as provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice directed that if Respondent seeks to contest imposition of his exclusion, he must file a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Because Respondent did not file a response, the Director determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and that exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish a 'genuine issue of material fact' to avoid identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: To contest the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the State, the respondent must file a response establishing a genuine issue of material fact that identical discipline would be unwarranted under the grounds permissible in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice required a response "containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Nebraska would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)." Failure to respond permits the Director to determine there is no genuine issue and to impose exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for wind-up (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order to wind up client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this limited recognition period Respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10040. The order explicitly ties the limited recognition to the 30‑day wind-up period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order, Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order plainly directs: "Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by this Final Order."

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to publish Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette identifying the practitioner, registration number, grounds for exclusion, and the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes the exact text authorized for publication in the Official Gazette (NOTICE OF EXCLUSION) describing the practitioner's name, registration number, reason for exclusion, the state-court findings, statutory/regulatory citations, and the date the exclusion begins. It also references posting disciplinary decisions in OED's Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs OED to give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary agencies and courts, and to the public, as part of reciprocal-discipline procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 'while excluded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states simply that the Respondent must comply with § 11.58 during the exclusion period; the Final Order does not reproduce § 11.58's text but imposes it as a compliance obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires compliance with the regulatory reinstatement procedures set out in § 11.60 when seeking to be reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for the action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites statutory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32) and USPTO regulations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59) as the legal basis for the exclusion and related notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service under 37 C.F.R. § 11.11
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificate of Service certifies mailing of the Final Order by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11 and to any other addresses where OED believes respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a Certificate of Service block showing compliance with mailing/service requirements and references the respondent addresses used for service.
